title: A tour of the window
summary: The ribbon, Quick Access Toolbar, formula bar, Name Box, status bar and Backstage view.
objectives: Find the ribbon’s tabs and groups, and the Quick Access Toolbar.
Use the Name Box and the formula bar.
Read Sum, Average and Count in the status bar.
Open Backstage view from the File tab.

slides.h: The Excel window at a glance
p: Every Excel window has the same seven parts. Learn them once and you can find your way on any computer.
Top: tabs and the ribbon of buttons.
Middle: the Name Box, the formula bar and the grid.
Bottom: sheet tabs and the status bar.
In real life: Excel 2016, 2021 or Microsoft 365: they all have these parts, so this map works wherever you work.

legend: **Ribbon**: the buttons for the chosen tab
**Name Box**: the address of the active cell
**Formula bar**: what is really inside that cell
**Status bar**: quick maths on what you select

slides.h: The ribbon: tabs, then groups, then buttons
p: Click a **tab** and the ribbon shows its **groups** of **buttons**. Home has what you use most.
Can't find a button? Ask which tab's job it is.
Printing → Page Layout. Protecting → Review. Freezing rows → View.
In real life: Spent five minutes hunting for Freeze Panes on Home. It lives on View, because it changes how you view the sheet.

slides.h: Quick Access Toolbar: Save and Undo, always there
p: Above the ribbon sit Save, Undo and Redo, one click away whatever tab you are on.
Undo is **Ctrl+Z**: your safety net.
AutoSave saves every change when the file is on OneDrive or SharePoint.
In real life: Deleted a whole column just before a client call. Ctrl+Z brought it back in one second.

slides.h: The Name Box and the formula bar
p: The cell shows the answer. The formula bar shows how the answer was worked out.
**Name Box** (left): the active cell's address. Type one there and press Enter to jump.
**Formula bar** (after fx): what is really inside the cell.
In real life: Never trusts a number until she clicks it and reads the formula bar: was it typed in, or calculated?

slides.h: The status bar does quick maths
p: Select some numbers and the bar at the bottom shows their Average, Count and Sum. No formula needed.
Perfect for a quick check before you write a formula.
On the right: the view buttons and the zoom slider.
In real life: Selects the day's bill amounts and reads the Sum in the status bar before he closes the counter.

demo.intro: Step through the window, one area at a time.

frames.say: The **ribbon**: tabs across the top, groups of buttons below. Home holds the everyday tools.
The **Name Box** (left) shows the active cell. The **formula bar** shows what’s inside it.
Select a range and the **status bar** does instant maths: Average, Count, Sum.
**File** opens Backstage view, where you save, print, share and export.

tasks.prompt: Click the tab you’d use to **sort and filter** data.

quiz.q: Which tab holds Freeze Panes and Zoom?
quiz.explain: Viewing tools live on the View tab.

quiz.q: What does the Name Box show when you click cell F12?
quiz.explain: It shows the active cell’s address.

quiz.q: You want to jump to cell X500. Fastest way?
options: Type X500 in the Name Box and press Enter
quiz.explain: The Name Box jumps anywhere instantly.
File opens Backstage view for saving, printing and sharing.

quiz.q: What does AutoSave need to work?
options: A file saved on OneDrive or SharePoint
quiz.explain: AutoSave saves continuously to cloud files; for files on your laptop, save with Ctrl+S.

points: The **ribbon** has tabs, groups and buttons; think about which tab’s job a tool is.
The **Name Box** shows and jumps to addresses; the **formula bar** shows what’s really in a cell.
The **status bar** gives Sum, Average and Count of any selection.
**File** opens Backstage view: save, print, share, export.
recap.cheat: Name Box = where you are. Formula bar = what’s really there. Status bar = quick maths.

cards.front: What does the formula bar show that the cell doesn’t?
cards.back: The real contents, such as the **formula**, not just its result.

cards.front: How do you jump straight to cell X500?
cards.back: Type **X500** in the **Name Box** and press Enter.
